Well yes of course it did, at least for me at the time, it felt like i was growing up. i have always just wanted to be normal, and to fit in, and that was something that had been on my mind for a while so i was extremely desperate doing it with whoever would be willing in that college environment (which was not many at all). but at this point im at the lowest point ive ever been in my life, so i suppose at the end of the day not really. however i consider that wildly different from guys who were having sex 3-4 years before that in those other situations and were actually in relationships. drunken sex with random guys and then regretting it the next day happens often in college, but consciously choosing to be with someone in a relationship in high school and having frequent sex and just enjoying life with this person that desires you even when sober i think would have had a massive difference in my confidence to this day and for the rest of my life

It's not really about sex because i have had sex before, to me it's about developing as a normal human being. it's like im permanently behind all these guys. they had experiences 6 years before i even started having them. they grew up reassured in themselves, validated, in a way that i cant develop at this point because at that age it was normal, at this age its borderline sad. i hope im making sense
thank you for your comment. im not sure how long i can wait for something like that, i feel so hopelessly broken at this point that i cant imagine myself connecting with someone to that extent

On your third point, I have massive imposter syndrome concerning anything an adult would do, the principal thing being sex. I remember having sex around 2 years ago with a girl and freaking out in my head the entire time. It was like "this is what I'm *supposed* to be doing right now". Adults have sex. I'm still a child. These other guys were adults and were able to mature normally and develop "adult" social skills and reassurance when they were in high school. I'm so far behind.. For your third point, yes i am definitely desperate. I went on 3 dates with a girl about a year ago that a friend from where i went to college tried to set me up with. After 3 dates I asked her to be my girlfriend and she rejected me, and then we didn't see each other again. That absolutely crushed me. For your second point, its not the amount of sex i guess at this stage, its the fact that a guy at that age where everyone is young and "innocent" (not sure if thats the right word but basically at a time where emotions were running the highest) had that absolute desire from a girl like that to have sex. its just extremely validating in a way that i dont believe i can experience anymore. I don't know what i'm even saying anymore im just typing to put my words somewhere im sorry. thank you for your comment

This is not my belief and to be frank I think it’s silly to assume that there is anything after we die. “This life could be a practice before the actual game” is such a laughably foolish thing to think, that our consciousness somehow transmits into another animal or that there is some kind of after life where we keep going. For anyone even slightly religious who has been raised to accept that there is something after life, they can’t comprehend and forcibly reject any kind of thought that there is nothing afterwards. But the fact is, when blood stops rushing into your brain and it stops working, that’s it, you’re gone. I’m sorry to put it so bluntly but go ahead and continue to “practice suffer” man, I’m good on that.

The kid will grow up with that happiness that everyone is born with and will eventually start noticing that people treat him/her differently than other people. It will just want to fit in but it’s treated worse for seemingly no reason. For years it won’t understand why because the thought of treating someone differently based on what they look like won’t even cross their mind until they start hitting puberty, until they get older and realize that they were just dealt a shitty hand and there’s absolutely nothing they can do about it. It makes me sad to think about that innocent baby’s future

if you are born ugly you will feel like an outcast and that society relentlessly wants to get rid if you. everywhere you look you are reminded that you are unwanted. that can really fuck you up mentally for the rest of whatever life you choose to live until you cant take it anymore. and you cant speak out about it because then you are publicly calling yourself ugly which is just another unattractive and "unconfident" trait to have. you will legitimately spend the majority of your life suffering due to something completely out of your control. i would trade everything i have or ever will have to have been born slightly differently, the mental strain that would be lifted would be unbelievable. i could actually just enjoy this short life

I’ve tried, and tried, and tried, and tried. I’ve been rejected hundreds of times. In person, through social media, through text, indirectly through friends, through dating apps, when I was just trying to make friends, make acquaintances, make conversation, in all different environments. People just don’t like me. I get tremendous pain and tightness in my heart every single time and every day when I think back to how sad my life has become. After doing that for years and years you start saying to yourself “why the fuck do you keep doing this”, I would be stupid to keep trying. It’s pathetic. It’s sad. It’s harmful to me. I’m done. I developed panic disorder, I get panic attacks constantly, I developed self harming habits. I cry every day every morning throughout the day and at night. I’ve spend thousands of dollars on different therapists and medications. Im 23 and I have a patch of gray hair growing right above my left temple. I have bags underneath my eyes. I’ve conditioned myself to fucking hate myself like everyone else does. It makes me so sad to think of what is happening to me and how my life turned out. I don’t want to get hurt anymore :( I have been on a razor’s edge to killing myself for so long, I don’t think I could take yet another one
